hypothesis: A structured, quantum-aware SOC/SIEM integration layer that normalizes alerts, enriches them with quantum-specific context, and exposes them via standard SOC-friendly interfaces (JSON events, REST APIs, and webhooks) will reduce median incident triage time (MTTR) and missed-incident rate, at the cost of an acceptable and measurable increase in alert volume and SIEM ingestion load, compared to a naive integration that forwards raw model outputs as generic anomalies.

baseline.name: Naive SOC/SIEM integration of quantum detection alerts
baseline.description: The AI-based quantum detection pipeline (from Chapter 10) pushes alerts directly into a mock SIEM or log collector as generic anomaly events without quantum-specific fields or SOC-aligned severities. Mapping to SOC concepts is minimal: alerts contain only generic fields like timestamp, source, model_score, and free-text description. No dedicated alert enrichment, no playbook mapping, and no quantum channel health dashboard are provided. SOC triage is simulated using a simple analyst script that reads from a generic alert index and decides on actions without structured guidance or pre-linked playbooks.

alert_schema.notes: No explicit quantum metrics (QBER, key_rate), no severity mapping, no correlation_id to classical events.

siem_ingest.format: Line-delimited JSON, one alert per line
siem_ingest.storage: Mock SIEM backend storing events in a single 'alerts' collection or index

ticketing.behavior: No automatic ticket creation. A separate script can be run to manually inspect alerts but does not create structured incidents by default.

dashboards.status: None specific to quantum; generic alert count over time only.

treatment.name: Quantum-aware SOC/SIEM integration with enrichment and playbooks
treatment.description: The same AI-based quantum detection pipeline is integrated via a quantum-aware alert normalization and enrichment service that emits SOC-aligned events. Alerts include structured quantum metrics and context, normalized severities, and references to specific playbooks. A mock SIEM receives these enriched alerts into dedicated indexes, auto-creates tickets based on rules, and exposes a focused dashboard for quantum channel health and threats. Triage workflows are tested via scripted analyst drills operating on this enriched view.

alert_schema.notes: Severity is mapped to SOC levels (e.g., low/medium/high/critical). playbook_id and labels enable direct linkage into triage workflows and dashboards.

functions: Map model_score to severity via configurable thresholds and risk rules.
Join quantum metrics (QBER, key rate, channel health) from telemetry store keyed by channel_id and timestamp.
Join classical context (IP, device_id) using correlation_id or time-window joins with classical logs.
Assign playbook_id and recommended_actions based on sim_attack_type and severity.

siem_ingest.format: Line-delimited JSON, one enriched alert per line
siem_ingest.storage: Mock SIEM backend with separate indexes: 'quantum_alerts', 'classical_events', 'incidents'

ticketing.behavior: Automatic incident creation for alerts with severity >= configurable threshold (e.g., high). Each incident includes linked alerts, playbook reference, and status fields (open, investigating, contained, closed).

panels: Quantum Channel Health: time-series of QBER, key_rate, and alert density per channel_id.
Threat Overview: counts of alerts by severity, sim_attack_type, and playbook_id.
MTTR and Workflow KPIs: median and distribution of triage times per incident, number of steps executed vs. recommended_actions.
dashboards.implementation: Simple web UI (e.g., Flask + JavaScript) or notebook-based dashboards reading from mock SIEM collections.

workloads.name: W1-simulated-quantum-attack-campaigns
workloads.description: Replay fixed, reproducible telemetry streams generated by the Chapter 6 simulator and processed through the Chapter 10 reference pipeline, covering a mix of benign operation, eavesdropping attacks, jamming, misconfiguration, and intermittent failures on multiple channels.

input_spec.source: Pre-generated datasets in the repository (e.g., data/sim_campaigns/campaign_*.parquet)

usage.baseline: Feed telemetry into the baseline detection pipeline and forward resulting alerts as naive events.
usage.treatment: Feed identical telemetry into the detection pipeline, then through the enrichment engine into the quantum-aware SIEM integration.

workloads.name: W2-simulated-incident-drills
workloads.description: Pre-scripted incident scenarios combining multiple alerts into logically coherent incidents, to drive analyst triage workflows and measure MTTR and decision quality.

scenarios.description: Sustained QBER increase on channel_1 with correlated model alerts indicating intercept-resend.
Short jamming burst across channels_2 and channel_3 causing severe key rate drop and loss spikes.
Planned maintenance window with benign but noisy telemetry changes.

usage.baseline: Analyst or script interacts with naive alerts via generic queries grouped by scenario time windows.
usage.treatment: Analyst or script interacts with enriched incidents and dashboards to triage the same scenarios.

workloads.name: W3-analyst-triage-simulation
workloads.description: Scripted or semi-manual analyst interaction with alerts and incidents to approximate SOC workflows, with logging of decision timestamps and outcomes.

analyst_profiles.rules: Rule-based triage using model_score thresholds and free-text pattern matching for naive alerts.
Rule-based triage using severity, sim_attack_type, playbook_id, and quantum context.

usage.baseline: Run analyst_script_naive over naive alert stream; record triage events.
usage.treatment: Run analyst_script_enriched over enriched alerts/incidents; record triage events.

data_controls: Use exactly the same telemetry inputs (same simulator seeds and dataset files) for baseline and treatment runs.
Freeze detection model parameters (weights, thresholds) between baseline and treatment; no retraining between conditions.
Ensure alert scoring thresholds in the detection pipeline are identical for baseline and treatment.
environment_controls: Run baseline and treatment on the same hardware type (CPU/GPU configuration) and OS image.
Pin Python and library versions (FastAPI/Flask, pandas, numpy, PyTorch, HTTP client libraries) using a locked requirements.txt or Poetry lock file.
Disable non-deterministic parallelism where feasible (set PYTHONHASHSEED, torch and numpy seeds, and single-threaded BLAS if needed for repeatability).
operational_controls: Use the same SIEM mock implementation for both conditions, with configuration differences limited to index names and routing rules.
Use the same triage scripts and underlying decision logic, parameterized only by the available fields (naive vs. enriched).
Repeat each workload at least N=5 times per condition to capture variability; randomize execution order (baseline vs. treatment) to mitigate temporal bias.

metrics.name: alert_volume_rate
metrics.description: Number of alerts emitted by the detection pipeline and ingested by the SIEM per minute, per channel and overall.

metrics.name: incident_count
metrics.description: Number of distinct incidents created in the mock ticketing system for a given workload run.

metrics.name: median_mttr
metrics.description: Median mean time to resolution (MTTR) across all incidents in a run, measured from first relevant alert timestamp to incident status 'closed'.

metrics.name: p95_mttr
metrics.description: 95th percentile triage time across all incidents in a run.

metrics.name: missed_incident_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of ground-truth incidents (from workload scenarios) that do not result in any incident being opened and correctly labeled in the mock SOC.

metrics.name: false_positive_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of opened incidents that correspond to benign scenarios (e.g., planned maintenance) or noise, relative to total opened incidents.

metrics.name: alert_to_incident_ratio
metrics.description: Number of alerts per opened incident (alerts_count / incident_count), as a proxy for SOC workload per incident.

metrics.name: correlation_latency
metrics.description: Time between arrival of an alert and completion of enrichment/correlation (availability of enriched alert in SIEM).

metrics.name: dashboard_query_latency
metrics.description: Time to render standard dashboard views (quantum channel health, threat overview) under test query loads.

metrics.name: analyst_steps_per_incident
metrics.description: Number of discrete triage actions (queries, drilldowns, state transitions) executed per incident by the simulated analyst scripts.

primary.description: The treatment's median MTTR should be at most 80% of the baseline median MTTR (i.e., at least a 20% reduction), aggregated across repeated runs.
Treatment should not increase the missed incident rate relative to baseline; ideally it reduces it, but non-increase is a minimum bar.

secondary.description: False positive rate under treatment should not exceed 120% of baseline, to ensure improvements are not purely due to over-alerting.
Alert volume increase under treatment should be bounded (≤ 50% above baseline) to remain operationally acceptable.
Additional enrichment and correlation overhead should keep per-alert processing latency under 250 ms on the reference environment.

exploratory.description: Investigate whether enriched alerts and playbooks reduce the number of steps needed to close an incident.

failure_modes.name: Excessive_alert_volume
failure_modes.description: Treatment generates significantly higher alert volume (e.g., more than 2x baseline), leading to alert fatigue in a real SOC.
failure_modes.detection: Compare alert_volume_rate and alert_to_incident_ratio; flag if treatment/baseline ratio exceeds 2.0.

failure_modes.name: Increased_missed_incidents
failure_modes.description: Enrichment or mapping errors cause ground-truth incidents to be dropped or incorrectly grouped, increasing missed_incident_rate.
failure_modes.detection: Compute missed_incident_rate per scenario; flag if treatment > baseline for any scenario by a significant margin (e.g., +10 percentage points).

failure_modes.name: High_correlation_latency
failure_modes.description: Enrichment engine introduces unacceptable processing delays, making alerts unsuitable for near-real-time response.
failure_modes.detection: Monitor correlation_latency; flag if p95 correlation_latency exceeds 500 ms or if it doubles compared to baseline SIEM ingestion latency.

failure_modes.name: Overloaded_mock_siem
failure_modes.description: Increased event complexity causes the mock SIEM to degrade significantly (e.g., dashboard_query_latency grows beyond specified bounds).
failure_modes.detection: Measure dashboard_query_latency under standardized load; flag if p95 > 1000 ms or error rates increase materially.

failure_modes.name: Playbook_misclassification
failure_modes.description: Incorrect mapping of alerts to playbooks (wrong sim_attack_type or missing quantum context) leads to inappropriate recommended actions.
failure_modes.detection: During W2 scenario drills, compare playbook_id and recommended_actions against ground_truth incident_type; flag mismatches.

hardware.cpu: 4 vCPUs or 4-core CPU (e.g., Intel x86_64 or ARM64 equivalent)
hardware.notes: GPU not required; detection model is assumed to run on CPU for this integration experiment, reusing pre-trained models where needed.

software.os: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or equivalent) or macOS 13+; Windows 11 with WSL2 acceptable.
dependencies: fastapi==0.111.0 or flask==3.0.3 (one of these for APIs)
mock_siem_components: Lightweight HTTP ingestion service implemented in Python (FastAPI/Flask) with endpoints /ingest/alerts-naive and /ingest/alerts-quantum-aware.
In-memory or file-backed storage (e.g., SQLite or simple JSONL files) to represent SIEM indexes.
Simple web dashboard or Jupyter notebooks to visualize metrics and support queries.
